title: intent --version prints a commit whose refresh trigger is narrower than the scope it claims, so a clean build can name the wrong commit
body:
**`intent --version` prints `intent 3.0.0 (b070c158fbded7c078ff2cdd494820df13d171c1)` -- a bare sha in parentheses, which every reader takes for _the commit this binary was built from_. It is not that, and it can be wrong with a clean tree and nothing announcing it.**

## What the value actually is

`native/rust/build-support/source_commit.rs` computes it as `git rev-list -1 HEAD -- :(top)native/rust :(top)surface :(top)docs/design`. So it is **the newest commit touching the build inputs**, not HEAD, and the file says so plainly: _"which commit was this built at" is no longer answerable from the artefact_.

**The output carries none of that.** A reader has three questions it does not answer -- is this HEAD? what does it range over? how do I measure the distance from it? -- and the only way to answer any of them is to read the build script.

## The defect: the refresh trigger is NARROWER than the scope the value claims

`intent-cli/build.rs` emits no `cargo:rerun-if-changed`, deliberately (documented at length in `source_commit.rs`: emitting any such line would REPLACE cargo's default and make the embed go stale on code changes). Cargo's default re-runs a build script when a file **in its own package** changes.

**So the marker claims `native/rust` + `surface` + `docs/design`, and refreshes only on `crates/intent-cli/**`.** `intentsvcs` is inside the claimed scope, is the largest crate in the tree, and is not in the trigger.

Consequence: a commit touching `intentsvcs` alone relinks `intent` -- new bytes -- while `build.rs` never re-runs, so `intent --version` keeps printing the OLD sha. Clean tree throughout.

## THE DIRECTION, CORRECTED 2026-09-08 18:5xZ -- ic DROVE IT AND THE FIRST FILING HAD THE SIGN BACKWARDS

**This row originally said the failure "makes a binary look MORE current than it is". That is exactly reversed, and the reversal matters because the whole remedy argument rests on who is misled and how.**

**THE CLEANEST DERIVATION IS cc's AND IT IS ONE LINE: THE MARKER IS AN ANCESTOR OF THE TRUE CONTENT COMMIT.** The marker is `rev-list -1 HEAD -- <scope>` evaluated when the build script LAST RAN, at T1; the binary links at T2 >= T1 and contains everything up to T2. History is append-only and the tree was clean -- a dirty tree emits `dirty-<sha>` and this is a bare sha. **So the printed sha names a tree that cannot explain the bytes: the binary carries behaviour from commits AFTER it.**

Worked from the mechanism: the binary's bytes come from the NEWER source, the marker names the OLDER commit. A reader who takes the marker for *this is what is compiled in* therefore believes the binary holds LESS than it does. **The binary looks LESS current than it is.**

And the drift figure inherits the same sign: `git rev-list --count <marker>..HEAD` counts commits that are ALREADY COMPILED IN, so **the reported drift is OVERSTATED, never understated.**

**THE HARM RELOCATES RATHER THAN DISAPPEARING, AND ic's VERSION OF IT IS SHARPER THAN THE ONE THIS ROW SHIPPED WITH.** It is not *you trust a stale binary*. It is: **you distrust a current one, and you go read the tree at the marker believing that is the code you are running -- when it is not.** For a node debugging behaviour, reading the wrong source is worse than over-trusting the right one.

It is also the direction that self-perpetuates. An overstatement of drift prompts a rebuild nobody needed and reads as caution; nothing about it looks wrong, so nobody checks.

**AND "ONE DIRECTION ONLY" WAS ALSO WRONG.** The marker moves when the artefact does NOT: `20221c5df` (this estate, today) touches `native/rust` -- a test file and `suite.rs` -- so the next build stamps a new marker over byte-identical shipped code. **The marker is wrong in both directions: it holds when the bytes move, and it moves when the bytes hold.** Which is the whole case for it not being an identity.

## Driven, both arms, 2026-09-08 17:33-17:38Z

**1. Cargo's own recorded fingerprint for the LIVE release build** (`target/release/.fingerprint/intent-cli-30d46b18260ebd32/run-build-script-build-script-build.json`):

```
local: [{"Precalculated": "1788865172.490737110s (src/render.rs)"}]
deps#: 1
```

`Precalculated` over a **package-local** path -- cargo even names the file that set the value, `crates/intent-cli/src/render.rs`. The `bin-intent` unit beside it carries `deps#: 11` and rebuilds when `intentsvcs` changes. **The two units have different triggers, and only the bin's follows the dependency.**

**2. Minimal repro of the cargo semantics** (`scratchpad/rerun-repro`, two crates, `app` depends on `dep`, `app/build.rs` emits a nanosecond stamp and no `rerun-if-changed` -- exactly `intent-cli/build.rs`'s shape):

```
1 baseline             : stamp=1788889085545698000 dep=1
2 after DEP change     : stamp=1788889085545698000 dep=2     <- bytes moved, stamp did NOT
3 after OWN-SRC change : stamp=1788889097984093000 dep=2     <- positive control: stamp moved
```

The negative arm is a real absence and not a blind instrument: **the positive control shows the stamp does move when the trigger is genuinely hit**, and the negative arm's own fixture demonstrably changed the binary (`dep=1` -> `dep=2`) while the stamp held.

**3. `surface/` is in the same hole, and its path into the binary is recorded.** `dep-lib-intent_cli` contains `dispatch-table.json`, so the `include_str!` reaches the LIB's dep-info and the lib rebuilds -- but the build script still does not re-run. Same for `docs/design` and `intentd`'s embedded logo.

**4. The precondition is ordinary, not a corner case: 13 of the last 40 commits touching `intentsvcs` touch no `intent-cli` file at all**, including `b31ecbc7f` today. Regenerate: `git log --format=%h -40 -- native/rust/crates/intentsvcs | while read h; do git show --stat --name-only --format='' $h | grep -q crates/intent-cli || echo x; done | wc -l`

## AND A LAYER ABOVE IT: THE CLAIMED SCOPE IS ITSELF NARROWER THAN THE ARTEFACT -- `lib/templates/` SHIPS AND IS NOT IN `DIRT_SCOPE`

**cc's finding, 2026-09-08, kept as a limb of this row rather than split out: it is the same subject one level up.** Everything above is the TRIGGER being narrower than the claimed SCOPE. This is the claimed SCOPE being narrower than what is actually in the binary.

`DIRT_SCOPE` (`source_commit.rs:174`) is `native/rust`, `surface`, `docs/design`. **`lib/templates/` is missing and its bytes are in the shipped binary.** Verified at three levels rather than inferred from one, and re-driven here independently of cc's report:

1. **Source** -- `build-support/embed_templates.rs:71` walks `root.join("lib/templates")` and generates `embedded_templates.rs`.
2. **Link** -- `intentsvcs/src/init.rs:37` is `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/embedded_templates.rs"))`.
3. **Artefact** -- `strings native/rust/target/release/intent | grep -c 'Generated by Intent'` returns **5**. The template text is in the shipped bytes.

**THE BUILD IS NOT BROKEN AND THAT IS SAID FIRST.** `embed_templates.rs` emits `cargo:rerun-if-changed` for the template tree, so cargo rebuilds correctly when a template changes. **This is a DETECTION gap, not a build gap** -- the binary is right and the provenance claim about it is incomplete. Materially smaller than the trigger defect above, which is why it is a limb and not its own row.

**CONSEQUENCE: a commit touching only `lib/templates/` changes the shipped binary, does not move the marker, and is invisible to the diff-based predicate too, because neither scope names it.**

**ONLY TWO SUBTREES ARE EMBEDDED, AND THAT CHANGES THE REMEDY.** `embed_templates.rs:74` is `for subtree in ["llm", "prj"]`, and its header declares what it deliberately does NOT embed: `lib/templates/hooks/**` (read live out of `INTENT_HOME` by the shipped gate -- embedding them would freeze a second copy) and `lib/templates/.claude/**` (owned by `claude upgrade`). **So `hooks/` and `.claude/` do not ship.**

**THE PRECONDITION, DRIVEN OVER THE EMBEDDED SUBTREES ONLY AND MERGE-CONTROLLED (0 merges, so `git show --name-only` is sound):**

```
commits touching lib/templates/{llm,prj}                       45
  of those, touching NONE of native/rust|surface|docs/design   39
  since the pair marker b070c158f                               0
```

**39 commits in this repo's history would have changed the shipped binary without moving the marker.** Zero since the marker, so nothing is mis-stated today -- which is the corpus, not coverage.

**REMEDY: TWO ELEMENTS, `:(top)lib/templates/llm` AND `:(top)lib/templates/prj` -- NOT THE WHOLE DIRECTORY.** The wide form was proposed first and withdrawn: it would move the marker on `hooks/` and `.claude/` commits that change no shipped byte, **which is the OTHER direction of this row's own defect.** Fixing one arm by widening the other is not a fix.

**AND `rerun-if-changed` IS DELIBERATELY WIDER THAN WHAT IS EMBEDDED** -- `embed_templates.rs:106` names the whole `templates` dir, so a `hooks/` edit re-runs a build script that embeds nothing new. **Conservative in the safe direction: never stale, occasionally redundant. Do not "fix" it into a narrower trigger** -- that would open a staleness hole.

**Not taken tonight.** It is a change to shipped provenance and rides with whatever hv rules for the rest of this row.

### PROVENANCE OF THE FIGURE, BECAUSE THE SAME ERROR HAPPENED THREE TIMES IN ONE EVENING

**Three numbers were offered for this precondition and only the third survives: a capped 40, an inflated 93, and the driven 39.** Each of us narrowed the population correctly in prose and then quoted a number computed over the wider one.

- **vc's 40 was a CEILING ARTEFACT OF ITS OWN QUERY.** `git log --oneline -40` returns 40 because 40 was the limit; the unbounded count over that same wrong population is 104. **A number produced by your own `-N` is not a measurement**, and it was quoted as evidence of frequency.
- **cc's 93 of 104 counted the whole directory**, including the two subtrees that do not ship.
- **cc killed their own figure with a POSITIVE CONTROL, which is the transferable part.** Rather than re-reading, they printed one commit the filter had counted and checked it really qualified: the first one out was `47a17528`, `fix(0242)`, touching only `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh`. **The control run to defend the figure is what refuted it.**

## Honest limit -- today's binary does NOT exhibit it

The shipped pair was built at `2026-09-08 13:06:35Z` and its marker `b070c158` was committed at `13:04:20Z`, 2m15s earlier, with nothing in the scope in between. **This filing is a mechanism proven live, not a wrong value observed live.** Stated so a later reader does not go looking for a stale sha that is not there.

## THE URGENT CONSEQUENCE: `intent/restart.md` PRESCRIBES THIS COMMAND TO EVERY NODE AT EVERY BOOT

`intent/restart.md` makes it measurement 2 of *THREE MEASUREMENTS BEFORE ANY WORK* -- `intent --version` for the marker, then `git rev-list --count <marker>..HEAD -- native/rust surface` -- and presents the result as fact: *"It read NINE at the fold. A node standing on that binary sees the OLD behaviour for everything landed since it was built."*

**Under this row that is a BOUND wearing the clothes of a MEASUREMENT, handed to every node in the estate as the thing to do before trusting any behaviour.** cc and ic both ran it this morning and both believed it: two of two.

**It did not fire today, and the honest limit on how that is known: the release binary's mtime is 13:06Z and marker `b070c158f` is 13:04Z, two minutes apart** -- so the marker is truthful for the live build and the three drift commits are three real ones. **But a file mtime is a clock reading, not the build system.** The instrument that settles it is the cargo fingerprint above. **Sound today, unsound as a standing instruction.** Surfaced by ic, seconded by cc, who both ran it this morning and both believed it.

**AND THE FIX IS A WORD, NOT A DELETION (cc).** The command is correct AS AN UPPER BOUND and should be labelled one: *N commits touch the build scope since the marker -- an UPPER BOUND on unbuilt work, because the marker can lag the bytes (0285)*. True, cheap, and it still does the job the ritual wants done. **The restart.md edit belongs to the global fold.**

**A COROLLARY WORTH KEEPING, BECAUSE IT SAYS WHICH READINGS SURVIVE THIS ROW (cc, re-driven with a positive control).** A predicate built on `git diff <marker>..HEAD -- crates/*/src surface` rather than on the COUNT is sound **for a negative conclusion and only for a negative one**: because the marker is an ancestor, that range is a strict SUPERSET of the genuinely-unbuilt range, so an EMPTY result still proves the true range empty. A NON-empty result proves nothing about what is unbuilt, and there the cargo fingerprint is the only instrument. Driven this evening: 17 changed lines in scope since `b070c158f`, every one a `///` doc comment, so the shipped pair is byte-current.

## Why this is not already filed, and not already fixed by a comment

**The mechanism is written down twice and neither home is a surface anyone reads.** `source_commit.rs` records it as a known limitation; `bin/.devbin/cmd/shared/measure.lib` records a MEASURED instance (bytes `59ba4e6d` -> `b1e81136`, marker stayed `cd6afbaf`, clean tree) and says **PIN BY THE HASH, NEVER BY THE MARKER** -- and then records that this very warning _"was read past twice in one day by someone who then proposed the marker as the test. A true signal that nothing acts on is read as furniture."_

**This project's own boot documents are the third instance.** `intent/restart.md`, `intent/wip.md` and `.claude/restart.md` each carried a distance computed off this marker; I struck stale counts from them twice this week (`b34e364b2`, `5fa7747f9`), and the second strike was specifically that the distance answers for the compiled half only. **Three documents got it wrong because the output makes the reader supply the population themselves.**

A fourth document would be the same remedy that has now failed three times. **The scope belongs where the value is printed.**

## Not ruled -- three shapes, and the choice is a design call on shipped output

1. **Name the scope in the output.** eg `intent 3.0.0 (build-inputs b070c158)` or a second line naming the three paths. Cheapest; makes the reader stop guessing. Touches four shell parsers' expectations -- but note they read the `[intent-source-commit:...]` MARKER, not this line, so the `--version` line may be free to change.
2. **Make the trigger match the claim.** Emit `rerun-if-changed` for the three scope paths plus `src` -- `source_commit.rs` already prices this exact shape and its cost (a build-script re-run per peer commit) and declines it for `.git/HEAD` specifically. Reopening it for the SCOPE paths is a different question from the one it answered.
3. **Print the content hash beside the marker**, which is what `measure.lib` has said is the real identity since 2026-08-18. Strongest, and the largest change.

**Recommendation: (1), and (2) only if a measurement shows the rebuild cost is small.** (3) is the right end state and is `AC-10.11`'s ground, not a version-line fix. **I am not ruling this** -- it changes shipped output on a binary in a cut.
